STEP 1 - Vessel type: flat square plate (white, rim band visible, flat centre, no inner wall).

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type: square plate, typical range 20-30 cm. This one looks like a medium-large dinner plate, so I estimate about 26 cm per side.
b) Reference: the blackberries and blueberries are about 1.5-2 cm across. The plate spans roughly 12-13 berry-widths across its width (~24-26 cm). Cue agreement gives ~25 cm.
Final width: 25 cm square, area = 625 cm².

STEP 3 - Food items (footprint and thickness):
- Scrambled egg: occupies about 18% of the plate, ~112 cm². Loose mound, average ~1.5 cm thick. Volume ≈ 170 ml x 0.8 = ~135 g.
- Fried/seasoned grain (stuffing-like, brown): about 12%, ~75 cm². Mound ~2 cm average. Volume ≈ 150 ml x 0.8 = ~120 g.
- Bacon: 3-4 strips, about 10% of plate, ~60 cm², flat ~0.4 cm thick, dense cooked meat. Volume ≈ 24 ml x 1.0 = ~25 g (bacon fat included, crisp strips slightly lighter; use ~30 g).
- Strawberries: about 6 halves/pieces visible, ~20 g each for whole-equivalent, roughly 5 pieces visible plus hidden below: 8 pieces x ~12 g = ~100 g (sliced halves, about 12 g each).
- Blueberries: about 25 visible, 1 g each, plus a few hidden ≈ 30 g.
- Blackberries: about 8 visible, ~5 g each ≈ 40 g.
- Raspberry-type fruit near edge: negligible, included above.

Total ≈ 135 + 120 + 30 + 100 + 30 + 40 = 455 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: the grain base and egg are already counted as mounds; no large hidden layer. Total stays ~455 g.

STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g:
- Scrambled egg (with butter): ~150 kcal/100 g
- Seasoned grain/stuffing: ~150 kcal/100 g
- Bacon, cooked: ~540 kcal/100 g
- Strawberries: ~32 kcal/100 g
- Blueberries: ~57 kcal/100 g
- Blackberries: ~43 kcal/100 g

Energy estimate: egg 135×1.5=203; grain 120×1.5=180; bacon 30×5.4=162; strawberries 100×0.32=32; blueberries 30×0.57=17; blackberries 40×0.43=17. Total ≈ 610 kcal.
